  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

  The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
  agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the
  Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to
  (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker, not to exceed a total of (8)
  eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is heard. In order to be recognized and
  present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the
  beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers
  are taken in the order slips are submitted.

  Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
  public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
  meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
  meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
  conditions imposed.

  Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an

Subject:  2025-27 Poet Laureate Recommendation

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the Poet Laureate Committee's recommendation
to appoint Charlotte Ward as the 2025-27 Malibu Poet Laureate; and 2) Recommend City
Council approve the two-year appointment term beginning September 1, 2025.

DISCUSSION: Since 2016, the Malibu Arts Commission has overseen the Malibu Poet
Laureate program, including the appointment of the Malibu Poet Laureate, poetry
programs, events, and anthologies.

The City's inaugural Poet Laureate, Ricardo Means Ybarra, served a two-year term from
2017 to 2019. While working with the Malibu Poet Laureate Committee (Committee), Mr.
Ybarra expanded poetry programming by leading several poetry workshops, conducting
the first Poetry Summit, producing the first and second editions of the poetry and art
Anthology, and attending various community events.

In March 2019, Ellen Reich was appointed to serve the next term as the City's second
Malibu Poet Laureate before passing away unexpectedly in May 2020. Mrs. Reich devoted
her time to teaching and conducting poetry readings for the adult population, reading
poems at various City events, and working tirelessly to promote the literary arts.

From October 2020 to June 2021, Dr. John Struloeff served the remainder of Ms. Reich's
term, serving as the City's third Poet Laureate. Dr. Struloeff conducted virtual poetry
readings, writing workshops and served as the editor for the first community poetry
anthology, A Place Like This.

Serving as the City's fourth Poet Laureate, Ann Buxie began her term in September 2021.
Mrs. Buxie continued monthly poetry workshops in partnership with the Malibu Library.
She allowed local artists to showcase their work at local parks and facilities by beginning
the program Verse About Town. For the first time, Arts in Education was offered at all

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 5.A.
 Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District Malibu schools, in addition to distance
learning classrooms. Mrs. Buxie incorporated various art forms at the annual Poetry
Summit, including visual art, dance, improv, music, and spoken word.

In September 2023, Nathan Hassall was appointed as the City’s fifth Poet Laureate. Mr.
Hassall advanced the Poet Laureate program due to his efforts with digital outreach. He
produced a website, videos, e-mail blasts, and created newsletters for his followers. Mr.
Hassall attended various community events to advance his efforts and create excitement
about the literary arts. He successfully coordinated two annual Poetry Summits, which
included the California Poet Laureate as the featured reader in 2025.

In late 2024, the Committee began formulating the Poet Laureate application and the
selection process. The Poet Laureate application period was open from April 7, 2025, to
May 18, 2025, which resulted in eight applicants. The Poet Laureate selection committee
reviewed and discussed the candidates and unanimously recommended Charlotte Ward
to serve as the 2025-27 Malibu Poet Laureate (Attachment).

At an early age, Mrs. Ward chose poetry as her vital means of self-expression. Long a
member of Malibu Woman's Club who delights in collaboration, she hosts a writing group,
participates in area poetry events, and attends Santa Monica College Emeritus creative
writing and literature classes. Mrs. Ward has also co-authored The Home Birth
Book, Doubleday; Simply Live It Up: Brief Solutions, Purposeful Press; and since 1991,
multiple editions of the best-selling gemology series: Diamonds, Emeralds, Gem Care,
Jade, Opals, Pearls, Phenomenal Gems, and Rubies & Sapphires, Gem Book Publishers.
She has edited many business projects, six books on life coaching, and three memoirs.
With a BA in English and a teaching certificate, University of Florida, and an MLS with
Distinction, Georgetown University, she holds credentials in the MBTI, Neuro-Linguistic
Programing, Photo Reading, and Success Unlimited Network®.

If approved, Mrs. Ward has accepted the nomination and will serve as the City's sixth Poet
Laureate from September 1, 2025, to September 1, 2027.

The Commission is asked to review the Committee's recommendation to appoint Charlotte
Ward as the 2025-27 Malibu Poet Laureate and recommend her appointment to the City
Council for final approval.

Dear Malibu Arts Commission and Malibu City Council,

The Malibu Poet Laureate Selection Committee has made a unanimous and
joyful decision for the City of Malibu’s sixth Poet Laureate: Charlotte Ward.

We want to submit her nomination for formal approval.

This was a unique and exciting candidate pool. We admired all the
submissions, their poetry, and their desire and potential to serve as

Charlotte Ward is our unanimous choice. Her poetry is compelling; we feel

Subject:  Arts Marketing

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and provide feedback on the marketing strategies of
art programs and events.

DISCUSSION: At its Regular meeting on June 24, 2024, Council approved Fiscal Year
2024-25 assignments for the Malibu Arts Commission (Commission). The Commission
requested that marketing efforts for art programs and events be reviewed. This aligns with
Assignment No. 3: Provide feedback regarding advertising, marketing, website content on
the Malibu Arts Commission website, and arts programs and events within Malibu and
outside City limits. The items below outline the marketing strategies used by the
Department.

Websites
The Commission website (MalibuArtsCommission.org) contains information on various
art-related programs and events coordinated by the City and other local art organizations.
The homepage layout includes flyers, videos, resource links, and links to categories such
as the current exhibition at the Malibu City Gallery, poetry events and programs, the Malibu
Library Speaker Series, and art-related classes. Website pages include an archive of past
art exhibitions, public art, calls for artists, and general information on the Commission.

Additional information about the Arts Commission is available on the City of Malibu website
(MalibuCity.org). Details include Commission meetings, agendas, assignments, poetry,
and the Malibu City Gallery.

City E-Notifications
The City offers users the option to receive notifications via email or text message on arts
programs and the Commission (Notify Me). Over 900 people have registered to receive
information. Staff typically send E-Notifications to registered users one week and two to
three days before an art program or event.

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item # 5.B.
 Social Media
The Commission has an Instagram account (@malibuartscommission) and Facebook
page (Malibu Arts Commission). Staff post graphics that advertise upcoming poetry and
art programs and video highlights from art exhibit opening receptions. Instagram has 949
followers with posts receiving up to 200 views. City staff posts graphics once per week on
Instagram and Facebook.

Large-scale art events are also posted on the City of Malibu's social media accounts. The
City’s Instagram account (@cityofmalibu) has over 20,000 followers. Postings are also on
the City of Malibu Community Services Department social media accounts
(@malibucommunityservices), with over 3,000 followers on Instagram.

City TV
The City TV3 Channel has program information on rotation and has featured art-related
pre-recorded events such as the annual Poetry Summit.

Print Publications
The Community Services Department produces and distributes the quarterly Recreation
Guide and City Newsletter (Guide). The Guide is mailed to all Malibu residents and
businesses and is also available at City facilities such as City Hall, the Michael Landon
Center, and the Malibu Community Pool. It includes information on the seasonal art
exhibitions and poetry programs.

The publication, Senior Center News and Views, is distributed monthly to 700 people and
includes details on art programs and the Malibu City Gallery.

Advertisements
Commission events and poetry programs are listed in the Calendar Section of the Malibu
Times. Additional advertisements may include a quarter-page full-color ad printed in the
weekly newspaper.

Press
The City’s media team assists the Department with writing and distributing press releases
to over 1,500 media personnel. A press release from Summer 2024 earned the City
special coverage of the “A Tale of a Seaside Town” art exhibition during the Fox 11 Good
Day LA Morning News segment, which reached over 12,700 people.

The City has partnered with KBUU, a Malibu radio station, to provide public service
announcements (PSAs) about art programs and events.

Partnerships
Malibu Library hosts several poetry programs throughout the year. Due to their
involvement, library visitors learn about arts programs. The Library also displays Verse
About Town poetry at the building’s entrance.

  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item # 5.B.
 Outreach Events
The Department hosts outreach tables/events at Malibu Bluffs Park each quarter. Staff
promote all recreation, enrichment, and art programs at various community events, such
as Malibu Little League and American Youth Soccer Association opening days. Additional
outreach is provided at school open houses, the public safety fair, and, the Malibu Farmers
Market.

Other
Staff create flyers, banners, and posters that are posted at Malibu Bluffs Park and used
on websites and social media.

The City also releases a City Managers Message, which includes information on all City-
related projects, including art programs and events.
